name: Prepare the annual cost budget
summary: Because the organisation charges its clients exactly what it costs to run, each autumn finance builds next year's operating budget and each client's expected share. The planning team sets the timetable and assumptions, the CFO and CEO set a cost envelope tied to the savings promised to clients, divisions submit headcount, technology and other requests, and executive sessions cut them back to the envelope over one or more rounds. Clients review their share before the Finance and Audit Committee and the Board approve, and the budget is loaded for monthly cost allocation. Late submissions, repeated revision rounds and the fixed dates of client and board meetings make up most of the elapsed time.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with about 242 staff and operating expenses that grew from about $117 million in 2020 to $157 million in 2021, all recovered from four client institutions.
baseline.notes: Spreadsheet budget model and templates fed from the ERP and HR system; no dedicated planning software.

trigger: The updated strategic and business plan sets the priorities for the coming year and the planning team starts the budget cycle.
end_state: The Board has approved the operating and capital budget and staffing plan, it is loaded in the ERP and allocation model, and divisions and clients have their figures.

volume.seasonality: One cycle a year, from late summer to December, ahead of the calendar fiscal year.

evidence.note: One Board-approved budget a year, as in the organisation file process map.

steps.name: Draft the budget calendar, guidance and templates
steps.description: After the strategic and business plan is updated, the budgeting analyst drafts the timetable, the planning assumptions (salary increase, incentive targets, inflation, exchange rates, headcount rules) and the templates each division will complete.

error.defect_description: An outdated assumption (for example a salary increase rate) left in the templates.

evidence.note: Calendar, written guidance and preloaded templates are the common first steps; timing after the plan is an author estimate.

steps.name: CFO sets the cost envelope with the CEO
steps.description: The CFO agrees with the CEO a top-down operating cost target that keeps the model manager's costs within what was promised to clients, including the year's savings target and the comparison with reference fees, and approves the guidance.

control.basis: The model manager cost governance: the business plan carries a yearly cost savings target and costs are tracked against reference fees agreed with clients

evidence.note: Yearly savings target and reference fees are described in the model manager's 2020 report.

steps.name: Preload templates with run-rate costs and headcount
steps.description: The analyst fills each division's template with year-to-date actuals and the forecast to year end, current and approved headcount from the HR system, signed contracts for technology and data, and lease costs, so managers only have to explain changes.

error.defect_description: A vacant position or contract renewal missed in the run rate.

evidence.note: Preloading a model from past results is described; effort is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investment office compiles the investments division requests
steps.description: The investment office manager collects each asset class team's requests for new positions, research and data, travel, deal pursuit and systems, and puts them in the template with justification for each increase.

error.defect_description: Requests double count positions already approved mid-year.

evidence.note: The investments division holds about 90 of 242 staff in the organisation file; the submission window is an author estimate.

steps.name: CIO reviews and ranks the investments requests
steps.description: The chief investment officer reviews the division's request with the managing directors, cuts or ranks additions against the investment plan, and signs off the division submission.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Technology and data prepares its budget
steps.description: The vice president of technology and data prices software subscriptions, data licences, infrastructure, consultants and the year's projects, separating run costs from project and capital spending.

error.defect_description: A project's licence costs left out of the run rate.

evidence.note: IT and data costs were a growing operating expense in 2020 and 2021; detail is an author estimate.

steps.name: HR prices the compensation plan
steps.description: The total rewards manager costs salaries with the planned increase, the incentive pool, benefits, the pension contribution and payroll taxes for current staff and every requested new position with its start month.

error.defect_description: Start months or incentive rates applied wrongly.

evidence.note: Compensation is the model manager's largest operating cost and drove the 2021 increase; method is an author estimate.

steps.name: COO reviews the operations and technology submissions
steps.description: The chief operating officer reviews investment operations and technology requests, challenges new positions and projects, and approves the submission for the operations, technology and data division.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Consolidate submissions and check completeness
steps.description: The analyst loads every division's submission into the budget model, checks headcount against the HR plan and contract costs against procurement, and lists missing or inconsistent items.

evidence.note: Late or incomplete submissions are common; share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Chase late or incomplete submissions
steps.description: The analyst follows up with the divisions that missed the deadline or left gaps, and updates the model as revised templates come back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the consolidated budget and client share forecast
steps.description: The analyst completes the model: operating costs by category, capital spending, the external manager fee estimate from forecast assets and fee schedules, and each client's expected share using the cost allocation keys and forecast assets by client.

error.defect_description: Formula or allocation key error in the model.

evidence.note: External fees and the client's share of operating costs are both charged to clients; method is an author estimate.

steps.name: Director reviews the draft against the envelope
steps.description: The director of financial planning reviews the draft against the cost envelope, the prior year, the savings target and cost per $100 of assets, checks the model's integrity, and prepares the issues for the executive sessions.

evidence.note: The model manager reports costs per $100 of assets; review content is an author estimate.

steps.name: Executive challenge sessions
steps.description: The CFO runs sessions with each division head and the executive team to go through requests above the envelope, deciding which positions, projects and spending to defer, cut or fund.

evidence.note: Several revision rounds are normal (median of five versions); round probability is an author estimate.

steps.name: Revise requests and rebuild the model
steps.description: Division heads send revised requests and the analyst updates the model, the headcount plan and the client shares and keeps a version log for the next session.

error.defect_description: An approved cut not carried into the headcount plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: CEO approves the draft budget and headcount plan
steps.description: The chief executive reviews the final draft, the headcount plan and the savings delivered, and approves it for consultation with clients.

control.basis: The model manager cost governance and tiered approval authorities: the CEO recommends the budget to the Board

evidence.note: Tiered approval authorities are described; the CEO step is an author assumption.

steps.name: Prepare the client consultation package
steps.description: The director prepares each client's view: its expected share of operating costs and external fees in dollars and basis points, the change from last year, the main initiatives and the savings against reference fees.

evidence.note: Budgets are developed with clients in mind and budgeting is covered by the client support agreement.

steps.name: Clients review the draft budget
steps.description: Client finance and investment staff review their share, ask questions in meetings with the model manager finance and relationship managers, and some take it to their own committees before giving comments.

next.condition: client asks for changes or more justification

evidence.note: The client agreement covers budgeting and cost management; review time and share with concerns are author estimates.

steps.name: Address client feedback
steps.description: The director prepares answers and, where agreed with the CFO, adjusts the timing of positions or projects or the allocation, and updates the model and client packages.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the board paper
steps.description: The director writes the budget paper: operating and capital budget, headcount plan, cost per $100 of assets, savings, client shares, risks and the recommendation, with the model summary as appendices.

error.defect_description: Paper figures differ from the model.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: CFO finalises the board paper
steps.description: The CFO reviews the paper, checks it against the executive decisions and client feedback, and submits it to the board portal for the Finance and Audit Committee.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Finance and Audit Committee reviews the budget
steps.description: At its scheduled meeting the committee reviews the budget, capital spending and staffing with the CFO and recommends it to the Board or asks for changes.

control.basis: Finance and Audit Committee mandate: review of the model manager's annual budget, including capital expenditures and staffing

evidence.note: The committee's budget mandate and its six meetings in 2021 are stated.

steps.name: Board approves the budget
steps.description: The CEO and CFO present the recommended budget to the Board, which approves the operating and capital budget and staffing plan for the coming year.

control.basis: The model manager Act and by-laws: approval of the budget, including capital expenditures and staffing, is reserved to the Board and cannot be delegated

evidence.note: Non-delegable Board approval is stated in the OSC order; a peer's board also approves its annual budget.

steps.name: Load the approved budget into the ERP and allocation model
steps.description: The analyst phases the approved budget by month and cost centre, loads it into the ERP for budget-versus-actual reporting and into the cost allocation model for monthly accruals and client forecasts.
outputs: budget in ERP and allocation model

error.defect_description: Monthly phasing error in a cost centre.

evidence.note: Loading the approved budget into accounting software for budget-versus-actual reporting is described.

steps.name: Communicate approved budgets and client estimates
steps.description: The director sends cost centre owners their budgets, HR the approved headcount plan, procurement and technology their spending and project lists, and each client its approved cost estimate for the year.

evidence.note: Recipients follow the organisation file process map.

exceptions.name: Late or incomplete division submissions
exceptions.description: One or more divisions miss the deadline or leave gaps that the analyst must chase.

exceptions.name: Draft above the cost envelope
exceptions.description: Executive sessions send requests back for cuts and the model is rebuilt, often more than once.

exceptions.name: Client asks for changes
exceptions.description: A client questions its share or particular increases and the model manager adjusts timing or justifies the cost.

exceptions.name: Committee or Board asks for changes
exceptions.description: The Finance and Audit Committee or the Board returns the budget for revision, which goes back through the executive session.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the updated strategic plan to the approved budget being loaded and communicated
benchmarks.population: Annual operating budget of a Canadian cost-recovery public-sector asset manager, 2019 to 2022

evidence.note: APQC's top quarter finish in 28 days and the 75th percentile in about 56 days from setting objectives; this organisation adds client consultation and fixed committee and Board dates, and the case also includes the two to four weeks between the plan and the budget launch.
The 2021 increase of $39.8 million came mostly from added personnel.

pain_points.description: Division submissions arrive late or incomplete and in many spreadsheet versions, so consolidation is repeated and errors creep into the model.

evidence.note: APQC recommends a single version of the truth and training stakeholders; median five versions.

pain_points.description: Fast headcount growth means first drafts exceed the cost envelope, and cutting back takes several executive sessions.

evidence.note: Operating expenses rose $39.8 million in 2021, mainly from personnel.

pain_points.description: Client review and committee and Board dates are fixed, so a slipped executive decision compresses client consultation.

evidence.note: Budgeting is covered by the client agreement; the committee met six times in 2021.

pain_points.description: The external manager fee estimate and client shares depend on asset forecasts that change before the year starts, so the budget shared with clients is soon out of date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemptions for the model manager and its investment pools)
sources.supports: The model manager Board may not delegate approval of the model manager's budget, including its budget for capital expenditures and staffing, or approval of the business plan and financial statements; after the initial funding agreement the model manager is funded through cost allocation and recovery from its members.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: Cost governance includes a rigorous business planning and budgeting process, procurement, cost allocation and expense policies with tiered approval authorities; the business plan includes a yearly cost savings target; actual and forecast expenses are monitored against budget and reported to senior management, the Finance and Audit Committee and clients; the committee reviews the annual budget including capital expenditures and staffing; costs are compared with reference fees agreed with clients; 2020 operating expenses $116.7 million.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: 2021 operating expenses $156.5 million, up $39.8 million mainly from added personnel; total costs $473.7 million (63.1 cents per $100 of assets); external management fees $291.0 million; the Finance and Audit Committee reviews and monitors the annual budget to support the business plan; six committee and ten Board meetings in 2021.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager operates on a cost-recovery model, its budgets are developed with clients in mind, and benchmarking data is used in long-term financial planning.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: An Implementation and Support Agreement between the pension client and the model manager covers the model manager corporate policies, asset pool development, budgeting and cost management; the model manager's share of operating costs is charged to the pension client on a cost-recovery basis.

sources.title: BCI 2021-2022 Corporate Annual Report
sources.supports: At a peer cost-recovery public-sector asset manager the CEO/CIO prepares the annual business plan and budget, the board approves the business plan and annual budget and meets quarterly, and finance streamlined its budget process.

sources.title: 4 tips for a faster and more effective budgeting process: Metric of the Month
sources.supports: APQC data from nearly 6,000 organisations: annual budget cycle time from setting objectives to a ready-to-use budget is 28 days or less in the top quarter, nearly twice as fast as the 75th percentile; median of five budget versions.

sources.title: Budgetary planning
sources.supports: Typical sequence: board strategic direction, milestone calendar, written procedures, preloaded model from past results, managers adjust their parts, aggregation and senior management review with several revisions, board approval, load into accounting software.

assumptions: One case is the whole annual operating budget. Division heads' submissions are represented by the investment office manager and CIO for the investments division, and the head of technology, HR total rewards and COO for operations, technology and data; other divisions' smaller submissions are folded into these steps.
Hands-on time for groups (division teams, executive sessions) is the total for the people named in the step; other attendees' time is not modelled.
The submission window is modelled as the wait before s04; technology and compensation work (s06, s07) runs in parallel, but the simulator still adds their hands-on time to elapsed time.
Revision rounds follow a fixed probability on each pass, so their number is geometric; on average there are about two executive rounds.
Client consultation is assumed to happen before Board approval because the client agreement covers budgeting and cost management; how formal it was is not public.
Stated FTE is averaged over twelve months; budget work is concentrated in about four months.
Web search capacity ran out while researching this file; budget practice beyond the sources listed is the author's estimate.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading).
